items.followUp: Draw the truth table for A + B (OR).

rubric.why: A two-input truth table must include all four possible input combinations.
rubric.description: Shows all four input combinations for A and B.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four combinations are shown.

rubric.why: For AND, the output is 1 only when both inputs are 1.
rubric.description: Gives the correct A·B output for each input combination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four output values are correct.

items.followUp: Write two examples of propositions that are both true.

accept: The sun rises in the east
rubric.why: A proposition is a statement that has a definite truth value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example of a proposition.

rubric.why: A second declarative statement with a definite truth value is also a proposition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid example of a proposition.

rubric.why: The internet is an interconnected network on a global scale.
rubric.description: Identifies the internet as a global network or network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its global, interconnected nature.

rubric.why: The internet connects computer networks and enables information sharing.
rubric.description: Mentions interconnected computer networks or TCP/IP and the sharing of information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the connected networks and information-sharing function.

modelAnswer: The internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks that use TCP/IP.
It enables computers to communicate and share information and resources.

items.followUp: What is a denial-of-service attack, and what effect does it have?

rubric.why: DoS stands for Denial of Service.
rubric.description: Identifies the attack as a denial-of-service attack.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or expanding DoS.

rubric.why: The attack disrupts service by overwhelming the target, making it unavailable to users.
rubric.description: Explains that excessive requests or traffic disrupt access to the targeted service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the disruption or unavailability caused by the attack.

modelAnswer: A DoS (Denial of Service) attack floods a computer system or network with excessive requests or traffic.
This can make the targeted service unavailable to its users.

items.followUp: Describe two warning signs of a phishing email.

rubric.why: A phishing website may deceive visitors by pretending to be a legitimate website.
rubric.description: Describes the website as fake or imitating a genuine website.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its deceptive or imitation appearance.

rubric.why: Phishing websites attempt to collect private login, personal or financial details.
rubric.description: Identifies the attempt to obtain sensitive information from visitors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a request for sensitive information.

modelAnswer: A phishing website may imitate a genuine website or use a fake login page to deceive visitors.
It may ask visitors for sensitive information, such as passwords, login credentials or financial details.
